chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim [from his father] from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Everything is permissible for you until you know that it is specifically prohibited, so you leave it on your own accord. And that is like the garment which you have bought, but it is stolen property, or the slave owned by you, and perhaps he is free and has sold himself, or was deceived and sold, or was compelled, or a woman under your authority (your wife), but she is your sister (by blood or milk) or your foster-sister. And all things are upon this principle, until it becomes clear to you that it is otherwise, or testimony is established regarding it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the default ruling for possessions and relationships in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the foundational juristic principle of 'al-asl al-hillah' (default permissibility), asserting that ownership and marital validity remain intact until specific knowledge or conclusive evidence ('bayyinah') proves otherwise. It illustrates this through practical examples like potentially stolen goods or a wife who might be a close relative, emphasizing that doubt does not negate permissibility in Shia fiqh.
